This targeting mechanism likely contributes to the observed effects on HL-60 cells, as this subunit is involved in the regulation of gene expression. The presence of a common target, DNA-directed RNA polymerase subunit beta, indicates a shared pathway or mechanism of action between Geldanamycin and etidronate in influencing HL-60 cells. The scores from the two paths, while not perfectly aligned, both point to a significant relationship, suggesting that Geldanamycin may exert its effects through a similar mechanism as etidronate on this target.
